text: A potential issue with failure training is that it increases the potential for overtraining and psychological burnout when carried out regularly over time (74). Izquierdo and colleagues (110) reported reductions in resting IGF-1 concentrations and a blunting of resting testosterone levels in a group of physically active men when failure training was consistently employed over the course of a 16-week resistance training protocol. Such hormonal alterations are consistent with chronic overtraining, suggesting a detrimental effect of repeatedly working to the point of failure. Thus, managing the amount of failure training, if it is to be undertaken, is important to ensuring progression over time.
